channel.title: Lawsuit Intelligencer
channel.description: Reporting and analysis on mass torts and the plaintiff bar.

item.title: The 2026 Mass Tort Map
item.description: A data-driven map of the 2026 federal mass tort docket: extreme concentration, the bellwether turn, and the erosion of Section 230 and bankruptcy.

item.title: State AI Enforcement Tracker
item.description: Every state consumer-harm enforcement action against a generative AI company: court, statute, counts, remedy sought, and status. Read from the filings.

item.title: The Preparation Does Much of the Negotiating
item.description: Elliott Portnoy, founding Global CEO of Dentons, on why some plaintiff-side MSO deals close at higher multiples while others stall, and how firms prepare.

item.title: Cross-Examined by Your Own Chat Log
item.description: Three courts have weighed a party’s AI chats, all of them made for the case. The ones a plaintiff made years earlier she hands over like any other document.

item.title: Juror AI Misconduct and the Limits of Judicial Delegation
item.description: A Georgia jury pool was discharged after a juror researched the case and shared it. What the Boles mistrial shows about where courts draw the line on AI in their own decisions.

item.title: The Expert Has to Be Right the Same Way, Forty Times
item.description: Josh Hyatt of Expert Institute on why testimony history sinks experts more often than credentials, what a bellwether expert has to survive, and what changes when an appellate court moves the admissibility line mid-litigation.

item.title: Arizona v. L'Oréal Moves the Hair Relaxer Fight to Disclosure
item.description: Arizona's consumer fraud suit asks what L'Oréal disclosed about relaxer cancer research. What that changes, and what it leaves to MDL 3060.

item.title: What Plaintiff Firms Get Wrong When They Buy Claimant Acquisition
item.description: Brian Beck of Typhon Interactive on intake economics, what to ask a vendor before signing, and why mass arbitration is a technology problem before it is a media problem.

item.title: The ChatGPT Log You Can’t Subpoena: Evidence at Intake
item.description: The Stored Communications Act bars civil subpoenas for ChatGPT content, and the order freezing deletion ended in 2025. What that leaves plaintiff counsel.

item.title: Otter.ai CIPA Ruling: The AI Tort That Skips the Output
item.description: Judge Lee held Otter.ai is a third-party eavesdropper under CIPA because it trains on what it records. The theory needs no product-or-content holding to work.

item.title: MDL 3026 Finally Has a Jury in the NEC Docket
item.description: Inman v. Mead Johnson is the first NEC case in MDL 3026 to reach a jury after three bellwethers died at summary judgment. Warning causation is the real test.

item.title: The Handwritten Line in the ChatGPT Leadership Order
item.description: Judge Schulman interlineated CMO No. 1 in JCCP 5431 by hand to preserve a pro se plaintiff's right to file. Why that line is worth reading closely.

item.title: The Case You Can’t Serve
item.description: A Senate bill would create a contingent-fee action against the President, his family, and federal contractors. Then it names an intervenor that does not exist.

item.title: The Docket the Panel Wouldn't Build
item.description: Twice denied an MDL, video game addiction litigation re-formed around a California coordination, scattered federal filings, and school district plaintiffs. The structure is now the story.

item.title: Federal PFAS Rules Contract, States Don't
item.description: EPA's 2025-2026 PFAS rollback collapsed a key litigation assumption. What changes for plaintiff lawyers when the federal anchor moves and states hold.

item.title: AI Due-Diligence Queries Are Reading Your Firm
item.description: Machine-constructed search queries are running litigation due diligence on companies and legal brands. What they look like and how to answer them.

item.title: ByHeart's Five-Month Sprint to MDL 3178
item.description: How the ByHeart infant formula botulism cases reached MDL 3178 in under five months, and what the hybrid injury-and-class structure means for firms.

item.title: Hair Relaxer's Daubert Gate and Intake Economics
item.description: MDL 3060's causation ruling will reprice an 11,500-case inventory. The Acetaminophen collapse, the Revlon channel, and what firms should underwrite.

item.title: Legion's Lawsuit Over the Fable 5 AI Shutdown
item.description: Legion LegalTech is suing the federal government to undo the export-control order that forced Anthropic to shut off its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models.

item.title: Fable 5 and the Section 230 Defense for AI Output
item.description: An export-control takedown treated Claude Fable 5 as a dangerous product, not protected speech. What that means for Garcia and the Section 230 defense.

item.title: Inside the AI Wrongful Death Docket: Pricing the Inventory
item.description: Plaintiff firms are signing AI wrongful death cases with no settlement history, no merits ruling, and no consolidation. How the inventory is built.

item.title: The First AI Infrastructure Class Action Against xAI
item.description: A nuisance class action filed June 9 opens a second front against xAI's Southaven power plant, already facing a Clean Air Act suit and possible DOJ entry.

item.title: Law Firm MSOs and the Indirect Fee-Sharing Problem
item.description: Private equity's path into personal injury law rests on one undefined word. No court has said where a management fee ends and fee-sharing begins.

item.title: Using AI in Court Briefs Without Getting Sanctioned
item.description: The AI sanctions docket is now its own body of law, and nearly every entry failed at the same step. A working guide to AI in court filings.

item.title: Mass Tort Intake Is About to Get Reshaped
item.description: The Eleventh Circuit's vacatur of the one-to-one consent rule is no all-clear. The pressure has shifted to TCPA class actions and state bar enforcement.

item.title: Editor's Note: Why Lawsuit Intelligencer Exists
item.description: What Lawsuit Intelligencer is, what it is not, and why it exists: an editorial publication on mass torts and the business of plaintiff-side law.
